relevance.rationale: Identity confirmed from the document's own title page (arXiv:0903.0853v3 [math.QA], local analytic classification of q-difference equations, three authors) and matches the seeded key. Eight citation sites, load-bearing, and the section locators VERIFY against the document: QOU/Mass/ThetaSlopeArithmetic.lean:62 cites '§1.3.2 (order/level), §2.2 (Newton polygon), §2.3.2 + Ex. 3.3.3 (level = slope difference)' — §1.3.2 is 'q-Gevrey levels' and introduces the space of formal series of q-Gevrey order s; §2.2 is 'The Newton polygon and the slope filtration'; §2.3.2 is 'The case of two slopes'; §3.3.3 exists as 'Computational consequences of the Birkhoff-Guenther normal form' (a subsection, not literally an 'Example', a trivial locator imprecision). The other seven sites (QGevreyOrder.lean:39,467; QAlienBridgeEquation.lean:51; DoorVParityNoIdentity.lean:39; RamificationParityMonodromy.lean:64; OddDecayWeightParity.lean:54; EvenFaceMassShadow.lean:44) cite it for q-difference formal classification / Stokes, which is the document's subject. Notably ThetaSlopeArithmetic.lean is HONEST about the open premise it leans on: it says in its own docstring that 'the grounding claimed for c1Slope = 1/2 runs through the Route-B ORDER, while RSZ would tie the slope to the LEVEL. Those cannot both be the Newton slope' and that the order-vs-level identification 'is the premise that remains'. That is a correctly-declared conditional, not a laundered one.

keyResults.statement: q-Gevrey order/level for formal q-difference series; the Newton polygon and its slope filtration; and in the two-slope case the level determined by the slope difference.
keyResults.useForFolio: It is the source of the order-vs-level distinction that ThetaSlopeArithmetic.lean identifies as the remaining premise behind c1Slope = 1/2 — i.e. the reference does not close the gap, it is what makes the gap precise.

proposedActions.rationale: Locators verified; the one file that leans hardest on it already states its residual premise explicitly rather than treating the citation as closure. Only nit: 'Ex. 3.3.3' is a subsection, not an example.
